events.title: Fire Follows You Home
events.body: A storm left a burning bush, and one of you has carried a brand back to the cave. The smoke stings, the elders call it bad luck, and the night animals disagree with everything. Keeping fire means tending it every single night, forever. Letting it go means warmth stays a rumor.

choices.label: Feed it all night
choices.quote: Warmth is a job with no weekends.

choices.label: Let it die out
choices.quote: The animals win this round.

choices.label: Teach everyone to carry it
choices.quote: Fire shared is fire doubled.

events.title: The Best Hunter Gives Meat Away
events.body: Your best hunter keeps handing out haunches to people who brought nothing. Nobody is starving and everybody is talking. Status, it turns out, is something you get by losing calories on purpose. The other bands are starting to notice whose cave has the loudest gratitude.

choices.label: Encourage the giveaway
choices.quote: Generosity: the original currency.

choices.label: Restrict distribution to hunters
choices.quote: Efficient. Unpopular. Predictable.

choices.label: Make it official: feasts on schedule
choices.quote: The party is now mandatory.

events.title: First Tool, Second Opinions
events.body: Somebody chipped a stone into an edge that actually works. The invention is spreading faster than anyone can claim credit for it, which is exactly the problem some of you would like to file a complaint about.

choices.label: Credit the inventor publicly
choices.quote: Naming things is the first trademark.

choices.label: Keep it secret within your family
choices.quote: Trade secret, era zero.

choices.label: Standardize the chip
choices.quote: Consistent edges. Zero genius.

events.title: Someone Dies (It's Not the End of You)
events.body: A hunting accident, thoroughly preventable, involving a bison and a decision. The band must decide what your name means now that one mouth carrying it has stopped. The lineage continues through someone smaller, younger, and deeply unqualified.

choices.label: Give the heir your unfinished tool
choices.quote: Management change.

choices.label: Redistribute everything
choices.quote: A clean slate costs history.

choices.label: Declare the death bad luck and move camp
choices.quote: Running is also infrastructure.

events.title: The River Has Two Banks
events.body: Salmon on one side, berries on the other, winter agreeing to arrive soon. Moving the whole band costs calories you may not have. Staying means betting the season on one bank's opinion.

choices.label: Move camp across
choices.quote: Logistics is destiny.

choices.label: Split the band
choices.quote: Two banks, two grudges.

choices.label: Build a platform over the shallows
choices.quote: Concrete before concrete.

events.title: The Stranger at the Fire
events.body: A limping outsider from a burned-out band asks to sit down. Letting them in costs food and might bring enemies. Turning them away costs something nobody can itemize until later.

choices.label: Take them in
choices.quote: New genes, new stories.

choices.label: Turn them away
choices.quote: The ledger remembers kindnesses unpaid.

choices.label: Take them in, make them earn it
choices.quote: Welcome aboard. Here's a spear.

events.title: Night Count
events.body: Something large has been visiting the camp's edge at night, testing who's awake. The band looks to whoever holds the fire-tending schedule, which is quietly becoming the most powerful job in the cave.

choices.label: Post rotating guards
choices.quote: Sleep is now a shift.

choices.label: Move the cave
choices.quote: Retreat: underrated.

choices.label: Chase it with torches
choices.quote: We are now friends with fire.

events.title: Ochre Handprints
events.body: Someone presses a painted hand on the cave wall and refuses to explain why. Others want hands next to it. There is a fight about placement, which is the first art controversy and will not be the last.

choices.label: Claim the best wall for the lineage
choices.quote: Branding, Upper Paleolithic.

choices.label: Open the wall to everyone
choices.quote: The first public forum was dirt.

choices.label: Paint over it with your own hand
choices.quote: Curation is violence.

events.title: The Long Cold
events.body: A winter that overstays by design. Stores say no. The body count says maybe. Elders propose walking south; the sick propose staying; the very young propose eating the seed stores, which is a proposal in the worst sense.

choices.label: Eat the seed stores
choices.quote: Borrowed from next year, at loan-shark rates.

choices.label: Walk south
choices.quote: Migration solves what math won't.

choices.label: Ration ruthlessly
choices.quote: Fairness tastes like bark.

events.title: Rival Band, Same Cave
events.body: Another lineage wants your shelter, and both of you have discovered that diplomacy is cheaper than the alternative, though nobody has written down either price yet.

choices.label: Share the cave
choices.quote: Roommates, era zero.

choices.label: Fight for it
choices.quote: The rent is paid in teeth.

choices.label: Trade instead: tools for their berry grounds
choices.quote: The first deal had no lawyers. Suspicious.

events.title: Dreaming About Tomorrow
events.body: The shaman insists the future visited her in a dream and said your lineage ends badly unless you stop doing something specific she refuses to specify until after payment. Half the cave is already nervous.

choices.label: Pay the shaman
choices.quote: Consulting fees exist in every economy.

choices.label: Ignore the prophecy
choices.quote: Skepticism: free, corrosive.

choices.label: Institute dreams as official policy
choices.quote: Governance by nightmare.

events.title: The Child Who Asks Why
events.body: A child keeps asking why the fire is hot, why the stars don't fall, and why the answer is always 'because.' It is exhausting. It is also, somehow, the beginning of everything. The band must decide whether questions are a resource or a nuisance.

choices.label: Answer every question seriously
choices.quote: The first curriculum was annoyance.

choices.label: Tell the child to ask the shaman
choices.quote: Outsourced epistemology.

choices.label: Make the child fire-tender
choices.quote: Prometheus got his start on night shifts.

events.title: First Granary, Two Policies
events.body: The surplus needs a building, and the building needs a policy. Hoard it and you're rich until the neighbors develop opinions about your walls. Feast everyone and you're beloved until winter audits the calendar.

choices.label: Hoard the grain
choices.quote: Wealth is stored envy.

choices.label: Feast the whole valley
choices.quote: Agalmic economics, threshing-floor edition.

choices.label: Grain temple: store it, lend it
choices.quote: Granaries were banks before banks had the decency to be invisible.

events.title: The Irrigation Question
events.body: Water is a mile away and the river disagrees with your field layout. A ditch feeds everyone for years and enslaves everyone for seasons. Somebody has to organize the digging, and that somebody acquires a title by the end of it.

choices.label: Dig the communal ditch
choices.quote: Civilization is a trench filled with water and complaints.

choices.label: Private ditch, private fee
choices.quote: Water tolls: the subscription model.

choices.label: Stay near the river, accept floods
choices.quote: Flood-based agriculture, flood-based mood.

events.title: Debt Is Invented
events.body: A farmer borrows seed against next harvest and discovers he cannot repay it, and that his daughter is legally considered collateral. The village looks to the granary-keeper — you — to decide whether debts have ceilings.

choices.label: Enforce the debt
choices.quote: Contracts are contracts. Say it gently.

choices.label: Cancel it publicly
choices.quote: Debt jubilee: popular then, expensive now.

choices.label: Cap future interest
choices.quote: Regulation: invented immediately before it was hated.

events.title: The Calendar Dispute
events.body: Planting day is a matter of opinion, and the two opinions are three weeks apart and both religious. Whoever arbitrates becomes, accidentally, the state.

choices.label: Back the astronomers
choices.quote: Science wins; half the valley sulks.

choices.label: Back the priests
choices.quote: Faith plants too.

choices.label: Plant both fields
choices.quote: Diversified eschatology.

events.title: Locusts Read the Ledger
events.body: Locusts arrive with the confidence of auditors. The stores will last two months if shared, four if rationed, zero if panic takes the gates off the granary first.

choices.label: Open the granary
choices.quote: Beloved, hungry, organized.

choices.label: Lock it, guard it
choices.quote: Walls work until they're the map.

choices.label: Sell to neighbors at famine prices
choices.quote: Every era invents this job. Nobody's proud of it.

events.title: Walls Around the Yard
events.body: Raiders took a sack from the outer field. The village proposes a wall. A wall protects the grain and defines who's inside it, which is a question with a sharper edge than flint.

choices.label: Wall the granary only
choices.quote: Protect the asset, expose the rest.

choices.label: Wall the whole village
choices.quote: Us, formally.

choices.label: No wall; armed escorts instead
choices.quote: Mobile defense, static resentment.

events.title: The Ox Breakthrough
events.body: Somebody harnesses an ox to a drag-stick and doubles the planted acreage. The landless laborers notice that their value just dropped, and they notice it loudly, at your gate, at dawn.

choices.label: Adopt the plough
choices.quote: Progress has a picket line.

choices.label: Tax the plough to feed the displaced
choices.quote: Compromise: everyone slightly unhappy, nobody starving.

choices.label: Ban the plough
choices.quote: The Luddite motion, six thousand years early.

events.title: Treaty of the Water Rights
events.body: Upstream villages control the river and would like something for the view. They propose a treaty carved in stone. Stone is durable; so are grievances.

choices.label: Sign their terms
choices.quote: Concessions today, maps tomorrow.

choices.label: Counter-propose
choices.quote: Negotiation is slow warfare.

choices.label: Build upstream reservoirs anyway
choices.quote: Facts are the best diplomacy.

events.title: The First Census
events.body: Counting people is boring until you realize the list decides who eats first. Your scribe now holds more quiet power than the harvest festival suggests.

choices.label: Count honestly
choices.quote: Truth: administratively convenient, politically fatal.

choices.label: Let the powerful undercount themselves
choices.quote: Corruption: the grease that runs the throne.

choices.label: Count households, not people
choices.quote: Hide children, gain surplus.

events.title: Priest-King Wants a Temple
events.body: The high priest proposes a temple funded by a grain tithe, promising divine yield forecasts accurate to within one season. The forecast is wrong every time. The temple, however, compounds.

choices.label: Fund the temple
choices.quote: ROI measured in obedience.

choices.label: Redirect the tithe to the ditch
choices.quote: Infrastructure vs. incense. Incense lobbies harder.

choices.label: Nationalize the priesthood
choices.quote: Now God reports to you.

events.title: Seed Selection, Season Forty
events.body: Decades of saving the hardiest seed are quietly rewriting the grass. The new strain yields double and tastes like wet cardboard, and it roots deeper when raiders trample the top.

choices.label: Commit fully to the new strain
choices.quote: Genetic monoculture: the empire's coming food allergy.

choices.label: Keep old strains as backup
choices.quote: A seed vault is a letter to the future.

choices.label: Trade seed as diplomatic gift
choices.quote: Soft power, literally grown.

events.title: The Elder Who Remembers Too Much
events.body: The oldest member of the village remembers three famines, two treaties, and precisely who broke each one. Writing is arriving, and there is a debate about which version of events gets carved. The elder has opinions about the editing process.

choices.label: Carve the elder's version
choices.quote: History: authored by the surviving.

choices.label: Carve the scribe's version
choices.quote: Accuracy is a faction.

choices.label: Carve both, side by side
choices.quote: Footnotes cause wars eventually. Worth it.

events.title: The Tin Route Delegation
events.body: The tin road — bronze's supply chain — runs through four kingdoms and a strait controlled by people with toll booths. Negotiating it requires sending somebody. A slave trader offers services cheaply and results expensively. Your own son would be trustworthy, and is also collateral.

choices.label: Send the trader
choices.quote: Cheap envoy, costly fine print. [Chronicle flag: lineage clause — resurfaces Era 11.]

choices.label: Send your son
choices.quote: Trust is a hedge with a face.

choices.label: Send neither; hire pirates as 'observers.'
choices.quote: Plausible deniability, Bronze Age vintage.

events.title: Debased Coin, Rising Expectations
events.body: Treasury math says the legions can be paid in coin with less silver in it. The legions have scales. Loyalty and currency integrity are on a collision course and both report to you.

choices.label: Debase the coin
choices.quote: Inflation: taxation's shy cousin.

choices.label: Raise taxes to keep the silver
choices.quote: Honest money, dishonest harvests.

choices.label: Cut legion size
choices.quote: Cheaper army, longer frontier, shorter life.

events.title: Write the Law Down
events.body: Judges have been improvising verdicts according to whichever family visits them first. A reformer proposes carving the laws in public. Literacy being what it is, 'public' means 'where the powerful must squint at it collectively.'

choices.label: Publish the code
choices.quote: Rule of law: predictability, priced per column.

choices.label: Keep law oral and clerical
choices.quote: Justice by subscription.

choices.label: Publish, with royal footnotes
choices.quote: The asterisk regime.

events.title: Roads Are Arguments
events.body: The treasury proposes paving the trade road. Paving wins the argument with mud permanently; maintenance loses the argument with entropy annually, forever.

choices.label: Pave the main road
choices.quote: Every mile paved recruits a mile of decay.

choices.label: Gravel everything cheaply
choices.quote: Slow and gritty.

choices.label: Privilege a toll-concession
choices.quote: Roads work; barons emerge. Net unclear.

events.title: Palace Accounts
events.body: The palace books show three treasuries, none reconciling, all staffed by relatives. An auditor volunteer appears — genuinely competent, structurally unwelcome.

choices.label: Hire the auditor
choices.quote: Forensics is a blood sport.

choices.label: Reconcile nothing; rotate treasurers
choices.quote: Confusion is a compensation plan.

choices.label: Appoint the auditor's rival instead
choices.quote: Loyalty over competence: the classic.

events.title: The Philosopher's Invoice
events.body: A school of philosophers petitions for state funding, offering 'truth' as the deliverable. Their tuition bill arrives quarterly regardless of truth delivery rate.

choices.label: Fund the school
choices.quote: Philosophy: useless, load-bearing.

choices.label: Fund only engineering topics
choices.quote: Grant money follows weldability.

choices.label: Tax their lectures
choices.quote: Epistemology now premium tier.

events.title: Plague on the Trade Road
events.body: Illness travels the routes faster than tin. Quarantine the roads and trade strangles; keep them open and the census files itself.

choices.label: Seal the roads
choices.quote: Quarantine: effective, hated, temporary.

choices.label: Keep trade open
choices.quote: The market's immune system is cruel.

choices.label: Cargo-only lanes, no humans
choices.quote: Smuggling will exploit this. Immediately.

events.title: Overextension Notice
events.body: Three frontier garrisons request pay, grain, and a reason to exist. The core provinces request lower taxes. Geography requests that you stop requesting things of it.

choices.label: Hold every border
choices.quote: Imperial overreach, textbook grade.

choices.label: Withdraw from the far province
choices.quote: Realism reads as betrayal from outside the map.

choices.label: Subcontract borders to client kings
choices.quote: Outsourcing sovereignty: excellent margins, terrible reviews later.

events.title: The Library Copy Problem
events.body: The royal library's scrolls are aging. Scribes can recopy ten percent this year: agricultural manuals, naval charts, or the epic poems that legitimize the dynasty.

choices.label: Copy the technical texts
choices.quote: Utility over glory; nobody sings about crop rotation.

choices.label: Copy the epics
choices.quote: Myth preserved, engineering lost.

choices.label: Copy a bit of everything
choices.quote: A compromise archive; mediocre at all things.

events.title: Corporations Begin Badly
events.body: Merchant houses petition the crown for legal personhood: the right to own, sue, and outlive their founders. Clever. Possibly catastrophic. Definitely profitable.

choices.label: Grant charters
choices.quote: Immortality, incorporated. Royalty pioneered it; nobody else could afford it.

choices.label: Deny; personal liability only
choices.quote: Owners answer for owners. Radically unfashionable.

choices.label: Charter one house, yours
choices.quote: Regulatory capture, age zero.

events.title: The General With Popular Support
events.body: A victorious general returns loved by the legions and the mob, in that order. History has a word for men like him and the word is not 'retired.'

choices.label: Triumph, then governorship far away
choices.quote: Promote him outward.

choices.label: Co-opt: marry him into the lineage
choices.quote: Family is the oldest HR department.

choices.label: Retire him. Firmly
choices.quote: The Republic lasts another generation. The rumors do too.

events.title: Coin Reforms, Third Attempt
events.body: Neighboring powers mint your currency as counterfeit, badly enough to undercut it, well enough to fool markets. Recoinage costs a fortune; tolerance costs the standard.

choices.label: Recoin with hidden mintmarks
choices.quote: Numismatics as national defense.

choices.label: Flood theirs with better fakes
choices.quote: Forgery: black-budget monetary policy.

choices.label: Free-market shrug
choices.quote: Let quality speak. Quality is slow and currently losing.

events.title: The Scriptorium Budget
events.body: Parchment is scarce, monks are patient, and the shelf holds choices: a farming manual, a holy text, or a Roman engineering codex. Each copy preserves a world; there is vellum for one path this year. [Callback flag: whichever is copied resurfaces in Era 9 as the digitized archive.]

choices.label: Copy the farming manual
choices.quote: Bread over doctrine. The harvest votes.

choices.label: Copy the holy text
choices.quote: Salvation ships today; agronomy deprecates quietly.

choices.label: Copy the engineering codex
choices.quote: Aqueduct theory, zero aqueducts.

events.title: Knowledge Decay, Routine
events.body: Three shelves have rotted past reading and the abbot confesses nobody recopied them since before his vows. Forgetting is not an event here; it's weather.

choices.label: Prioritize salvage copies
choices.quote: Manuscripts eat monks slower than wolves do.

choices.label: Memorize what you can
choices.quote: Human backups: redundant, mortal.

choices.label: Let it rot; record the titles
choices.quote: A catalog of losses is still a catalog.

events.title: The Hill Chief's Protection Offer
events.body: A local warlord offers sword-protection for the monastery's grain. His definition of protection overlaps significantly with his appetite, and his literacy is aspirational.

choices.label: Accept the bargain
choices.quote: Order has arrived. Order chews.

choices.label: Refuse; fortify
choices.quote: Stonework is prayer with hands.

choices.label: Convert the chief
choices.quote: Baptism: the softest conquest.

events.title: The Relic Economy
events.body: A bone arrives claiming sainthood. Believers arrive claiming cures. The relic's provenance is fictional and the pilgrim revenue is real.

choices.label: Authenticate the relic
choices.quote: Faith-based auditing finds what faith requires.

choices.label: Expose the fraud
choices.quote: Truth: a downgrade to cash flow.

choices.label: Sell authentication certificates
choices.quote: Indulgences debut early. The audit comes due; it always does.

events.title: The Viking Winter
events.body: Longships appear upriver with the precision of a delivery service. The monastery holds gold cups, jeweled covers, and zero swords.

choices.label: Pay the danegeld
choices.quote: Tribute: recurring billing with worse service.

choices.label: Hide the books, lose the gold
choices.quote: They take the metal; we keep the meaning.

choices.label: Resist from the tower
choices.quote: Martyrs recruit faster than survivors.

events.title: The Heresy File
events.body: A monk's marginalia contradicts accepted doctrine and, inconveniently, is correct. The bishop requests the notes. The abbot requests advice. The monk requests patience.

choices.label: Burn the notes
choices.quote: Heresy resolved, data lost.

choices.label: Archive the notes privately
choices.quote: The forbidden shelf is always the interesting shelf.

choices.label: Litigate it slowly
choices.quote: Councils: centuries of procedure, inches of outcome.

events.title: The Plague Parish
events.body: Illness walks the valley. The parish faces the same arithmetic as every collapse: flee and live with it, stay and possibly die with honor, or quarantine the village and decide who counts as family.

choices.label: Stay and tend the sick
choices.quote: Pastoral care, terminal pricing.

choices.label: Flee with the library
choices.quote: The books survived beautifully decorated funerals.

choices.label: Quarantine line at the bridge
choices.quote: Public health invented at sword-point.

events.title: The Lost Roman Road
events.body: Surveyors find a paved road still intact under three centuries of bramble. Clearing it restores a trade link; the local lord fears it also restores invaders' GPS.

choices.label: Clear the road
choices.quote: Gridlock returns; so does gridlock's clientele.

choices.label: Keep it secret, use it yourselves
choices.quote: Infrastructure insider trading.

choices.label: Leave it buried
choices.quote: The forest was a better customs agent than anyone admits.

events.title: Christening the Old Gods
events.body: The countryside still leaves offerings at the spring. Missionary strategy demands a choice: outlaw the spring, or christen it and let the old gods retire under new management, same duties, revised paperwork.

choices.label: Outlaw the old rites
choices.quote: Persecution: expensive enforcement of unverifiable claims.

choices.label: Rededicate the spring
choices.quote: Brand migration with 100% retention.

choices.label: Ignore both; collect taxes either way
choices.quote: Agnostic fiscal policy.

events.title: The Chronicle Continues
events.body: The annals break off mid-sentence during the last chaos. Restarting the Chronicle means choosing where to begin: glorify the gap, document it honestly, or imply the missing century was a collective hallucination.

choices.label: Begin honestly: 'here we lost the thread.'
choices.quote: Radical transparency, medieval pilot.

choices.label: Paper over the gap
choices.quote: Continuity theater.

choices.label: Date everything from the restart
choices.quote: Year One energy; calendar confusion forever.

events.title: The Wandering Scholar
events.body: A scholar arrives with a chest of manuscripts from the fallen east — Aristotle-shaped boxes, medical treatises, star tables — and wants lodging, protection, and tenure.

choices.label: Shelter him and copy his chest
choices.quote: Ideas crossed the Dark Ages hiding in trunks.

choices.label: Buy the chest outright
choices.quote: Acquisition beats logistics, usually.

choices.label: Turn him in as a sorcerer
choices.quote: The bonfire was efficient. Terribly efficient.

events.title: Harvest of Ashes
events.body: Volcanic haze dims the sun; the harvest fails across the continent. Every granary in Christendom is empty by Advent, and your preserved knowledge is worth nothing because nobody can eat a codex. Yet.

choices.label: Break the seals; distribute church stores
choices.quote: The reliquary fed fourteen families. Reportedly.

choices.label: Ration by labor roster
choices.quote: Work-or-waste: grim, functional.

choices.label: Trade relics for grain from unburnt regions
choices.quote: Sacred objects become commodities exactly once per collapse.

events.title: The Press Investment
events.body: A goldsmith's screw press is for sale: it sets type faster than any scribe and makes errors at industrial scale for the first time in history. Financing it means betting the ledger on cheap pages.

choices.label: Fund the press
choices.quote: Movable type: the original disruptive vertical.

choices.label: Fund the scribes' guild instead
choices.quote: Preserving jobs, preserving obsolescence.

choices.label: Own the paper mill upstream
choices.quote: He who owns the substrate owns the argument.

events.title: Plague Year, Two Doors
events.body: The sickness is in the city. Fleeing preserves the lineage and loses clients, commissions, and the archive's lease. Quarantining buys legitimacy at population's expense.

choices.label: Flee to the country villa
choices.quote: The great escape, with manuscripts.

choices.label: Quarantine the district
choices.quote: Rings around neighborhoods: public health, iron band.

choices.label: Keep the press running outside town
choices.quote: The epidemic slowed; the edition didn't.

events.title: The Patron's Dilemma
events.body: A banking family offers a fortune for a dedication: your name on their patronage, their accounting under your protection. Their money is laundered through art so thick you could frame it twice.

choices.label: Take the patronage
choices.quote: Beauty, mildly stolen. Standard terms.

choices.label: Decline on principle
choices.quote: Poverty has excellent reviews and terrible cash flow.

choices.label: Counter: fund a public library in their name
choices.quote: Reputation laundering, civic grade.

events.title: The Anatomist's Petition
events.body: A physician requests permission to study actual cadavers rather than authoritative texts, which are wrong authoritatively. The guild and the diocese have pre-registered objections jointly.

choices.label: Grant the license quietly
choices.quote: Truth by permit, after hours.

choices.label: Deny; fund text-commentary instead
choices.quote: Error, but error with tenure.

choices.label: Public dissection, licensed, ticketed
choices.quote: Education debuted as paid entertainment.

events.title: Index of Forbidden Pamphlets
events.body: A heretical pamphlet is outperforming your official publications three to one. The bishop wants a ban; the market wants volume; both use the word 'souls.'

choices.label: Ban it
choices.quote: Prohibition: worst-case marketing.

choices.label: Print it yourself, annotated
choices.quote: If you can't censor it, edit it.

choices.label: Let the marketplace of ideas brawl
choices.quote: Content neutrality, sixteenth-century rules.

events.title: The Double-Entry Revelation
events.body: A monk-accountant publishes a method where every debit has a credit. Ledger fraud drops forty percent overnight and rises again within a generation, now more sophisticated.

choices.label: Adopt it firm-wide
choices.quote: Books that balance: civilization's checksum.

choices.label: Keep single-entry for 'flexibility.'
choices.quote: Creative accounting needs creative recordkeeping.

choices.label: Require it of all clients
choices.quote: Regulatory standardization, vendor-neutral.

events.title: The Navigator's Speculative Voyage
events.body: A captain proposes a westward route to spice markets, requesting ships and offering wonder. Expected returns are either ruinous or historic, and he cannot honestly distinguish which.

choices.label: Fund the voyage
choices.quote: Portfolio theory, caravel tier.

choices.label: Refuse; watch competitors fund it
choices.quote: Discovery happened anyway. Not to us.

choices.label: Fund two rival captains
choices.quote: Hedged exploration: history's first dual listing.

events.title: The Forgery Workshop
events.body: An artist's workshop produces antique-looking antiquities that collectors adore and scholars increasingly authenticate. Revenue is strong; provenance is a fiction with brushstrokes.

choices.label: Shut it down publicly
choices.quote: Authenticity enforced, income arrested.

choices.label: Rebrand: 'in the antique manner.'
choices.quote: Truth in labeling; fraud in mood.

choices.label: Buy the best pieces for the public collection
choices.quote: Institutional laundering of institutional fakes.

events.title: The Star Table Heresy
events.body: The new astronomy's tables predict eclipses better than the old ones and place Earth somewhere embarrassing. Use the heretical tables and admit measurement beats scripture; use the approved ones and keep calendars wrong with confidence.

choices.label: Use the new tables
choices.quote: The data shipped; the cosmology lagged.

choices.label: Commission a compromise cosmology
choices.quote: Epicycles: elegant patches on a wrong foundation.

choices.label: Silently adopt, publicly deny
choices.quote: Hypocrisy: the interoperability layer of eras.

events.title: The Printing Strike
events.body: Type-setters strike over piece-rates because the press doubled output and halved rates per page, a development they characterize as 'the machine stealing bread.' Their argument will be recycled, with better suits, forever.

choices.label: Meet the wage demands
choices.quote: Labor peace priced per sheet.

choices.label: Import cheaper strikebreakers
choices.quote: Scabs: scalable labor arbitrage.

choices.label: Profit-share on volume
choices.quote: Align incentives before the presses align against you.

events.title: The Siege of the Library
events.body: Army or fire — the distinction stops mattering — approaches the region's greatest collection. Transport capacity saves a fraction. Choosing which fraction is choosing which future gets read.

choices.label: Save the technical corpus
choices.quote: Engines of the next era, mule-back.

choices.label: Save the literary canon
choices.quote: The soul of the age, catalogued.

choices.label: Copy the fastest-moving texts first; abandon the rest
choices.quote: Triage of memory.

events.title: The Copied Error Goes Viral
events.body: A typo in an early printed medical text — one dosage symbol transposed — is now in four hundred copies and climbing, because presses replicate mistakes with a fidelity scribes never achieved. Corrections travel slower than errors.

choices.label: Print a correction erratum
choices.quote: Corrections: free, ignored, necessary.

choices.label: Buy and burn the bad edition
choices.quote: Censorship of our own product. Efficient.

choices.label: Sue the compositor
choices.quote: Accountability theater; the typo persists.

events.title: Shares for a Ship
events.body: One hull is not enough for the voyage, so strangers buy pieces of it. The coffeehouse floor does the work no exchange building exists to do yet: shares change hands over cold coffee and loud arithmetic. What nobody priced is the second part — shareholders never leave. They send letters. They form committees. Your captain now reports to people who have never smelled a rope, and their patience has a shorter half-life than any provision aboard.

choices.label: Sell generously, answer later
choices.quote: Capital has no horizon. It has a meeting schedule.

choices.label: Promise routes you don't have
choices.quote: Prospectus: prophecy with a signature line.

events.title: The Charter Monopoly
events.body: The crown grants your house exclusive rights to a sea lane, which is a tax collected by you instead of them, minus the accountability. Monopoly profits land immediately, warm and heavy as bullion. Smugglers, being entrepreneurs with better boats, begin testing the clause-by-clause strength of the grant. Enforcement turns out to be a subscription service too, and the renewal fee is measured in gunpowder and grudges.

choices.label: Refuse and trade free
choices.quote: Principles: cheaper than cannons, briefly.

events.title: Passage Money
events.body: A broker offers to fill holds with desperate families: their passage paid in advance, their labor sold forward by yours. The ships leave full, the ledgers balance beautifully, and something bleeds out of the house's story at home in slow quarterly increments. Every clause of the contract is legal, which the broker mentions the way one mentions weather. The ledger's beauty is the point: every column balances, and none of them mention names.

choices.label: Grant nothing. No holds, no contracts.
choices.quote: Some cargo is an invoice that fights back.

choices.label: Middle passage terms: shorter bonds, higher rates

events.title: The Privateer's Percentage
events.body: A captain with more flags than scruples proposes commissions: his guns, your paper, rivals' cargo split by formula. Law, he explains with a bow, is mostly a flag you fly, and he flies several, seasonally. The math is excellent. The precedent is load-bearing, and you are standing under it. The harbor masters take their cut of the commissions and consider themselves uninvolved, which is the correct legal posture and the wrong moral one.

choices.label: Hire him to hunt himself
choices.quote: Poacher-turned-gamekeeper, maritime edition.

events.title: Plague Ship in the Downs
events.body: One of your own hulls sits at anchor with fever in the hold and bills of lading worth a season. The harbor wants her burned or buried; the cargo manifest wants otherwise; the crew wants absolution, available separately. Quarantine means feeding the sick and losing the goods. Sailing on means the goods arrive somewhere else's problem, wearing your flag. The crew stands on the quay afterward and watches the smoke, doing the arithmetic between cargo value and burial depth, and finding the two numbers uncomfortably close.

choices.label: Quarantine. Feed the sick, lose the cargo.
Sail on before anyone boards
choices.quote: The next port has heard worse rumors. Briefly.

events.title: The Longitude Premium
events.body: A bounty hangs over the western lane: build a seawatch that tells west from south, and every hull you own stops dying of arithmetic. A clockmaker with steady hands and unsteady rent claims she can do it. Every admiral says a spring watch will lie at sea. She says admirals navigate by superstition and lunch. The trials will take years and eat money at a constant rate regardless of results.

choices.label: Fund the clockmaker
choices.quote: Longitude: the original hard timing problem.

events.title: The Company Raises Its Flag
events.body: The trading house has grown a fort, the fort a court, the court judges, and the judges seals. Without anyone quite deciding it, you hired a proto-state that fits in a ledger. It provides law, roads, and violence in convenient bundles, invoices arriving monthly. Revenues rise. Sovereignty creeps. Somewhere a local ruler is studying your flag very closely and drafting correspondence.

choices.label: Cap the forts, keep the counters
Hand the courts to the crown

events.title: Cargo of Somebody Else's Silver
events.body: Galleons arrive heavy with mountain silver, and prices notice before anyone votes on it. Coin buys less each tide; wages chase rents; the accountant develops a twitch labeled monetary phenomenon. The silver is real, the wealth is debatable, and the inflation does not care whose mine dug it. Hoarding feels wise for exactly one season. The wise convert metal into land, warehouses, and favors before the next galleon clears the horizon, because silver has no opinion about its own purchasing power.

choices.label: Convert silver to land and hulls now
Lend against future cargoes at ruinous rates

events.title: The Cartographer's Error
events.body: A chart off by a hundred miles takes two heirs and a grain hull onto rocks nobody drew. The surviving pilot insists the coast moved. A survey expedition would take three seasons and make the mistake expensive to repeat; reusing the old chart makes it cheap to repeat, which is a different accounting standard, favored by optimists. The widows petition for the survey either way. The coast keeps its position; only the paper disagrees with it, loudly, at night, in fog.

choices.label: Copy the old chart, add a footnote
choices.quote: Footnotes sink fewer ships than coastlines. Statistically contested.

events.title: Missionary or Factor
events.body: The heir going abroad chooses her equipment: a bible or a ledger. Both convert populations, just to different currencies, and the mission school and the counting house keep adjacent books about the same village. The missionary learns the language properly. The factor learns it phonetically, for bargaining. Whichever you fund, the correspondence will shape the region for four generations. The village gets one schoolhouse and two histories, both carefully footnoted, neither of which will be legible to the grandchildren without a guide.

events.title: Blockade Season
events.body: Enemy sails choke the lane and the calendar does not negotiate: miss the window and the season's cargo rots where it stands. Running the blockade costs hulls and names. Rerouting through a rival's port works fine and creates a dependency with an opinion about pricing, exercised annually, in person, by their relatives. The factors price the delay into next season's contracts, all of them, including the ones that pretend the lane is open and honest as ever.

choices.label: Reroute through the rival port
choices.quote: Every shortcut is a lease. Read the renewal clause.

choices.label: Sit the season out, keep crews paid

events.title: The Ledger That Drowned
events.body: An heir kept double books, one per flag, and the ship carrying the wrong one went down with the only auditor. Now every entry is technically unverifiable, which reads as genius in good years and fraud in bad ones. The house trades on paper that means two things depending on the tide. Some clever successor will someday call it structured finance.

choices.label: Keep both. Edit history lightly.
choices.quote: Dual-currency household. Very modern, for it.

events.title: Shipwreck Salvage Law
events.body: Wreckers claim your spilled hull by ancient custom: they arrive promptly, help thoroughly, and leave with everything. Custom, it turns out, was written by the people with the fastest dinghies. You can write salvage law — precise, boring, enforced — or adopt their custom and point it at someone else's cargo for a while. The admiralty courts inherit the finished statute two centuries later, unchanged, which is the highest praise legal drafting ever receives.

choices.label: Split salvaged cargo with the crews

events.title: The Lineage Sprouts a Branch
events.body: A cousin-house across the ocean requests its own flag, its own books, and permission to stop asking. Half the family calls it mutiny; the other half has seen what six-month letters do to obedience. Grant the flag and gain a partner who grows independent on schedule. Demand tribute and gain a lesson in loyalty taught at cannon-point, invoiced to whoever wins.

choices.label: Grant the flag
choices.quote: Family, but distributed systems.

events.title: Articles on a Plank
events.body: A captured crew presents its articles: shares defined, injuries compensated, captains recallable, signed by every hand aboard, pirate paperwork with more consent in it than most navies. The admiral wants them hanged. The quartermaster who drafted the articles wants to be paid, in coin, per the schedule, and considers this the more important argument. The articles circulate among your own crews that evening, being read aloud, with commentary, by lamplight, which the admiral would classify as a second offense.

choices.label: Copy the articles for your navy
choices.quote: Best governance document this quarter: stolen.

events.title: The Talisman Below Decks
events.body: The Custodian comes aboard with the fire brand wrapped in oilcloth and stowed below, and calls it insurance with better premiums than yours. She has carried it through more crossings than the ship has had captains. When the chaplain objects to relics, she asks what the figurehead is. He has no answer that survives contact with her tone. The brand stays. The crew prays to both.

choices.label: Give the Custodian a cabin and deference
Stow the relic with the cargo
choices.quote: The relic noticed. The relic has a memory.

choices.label: Ask her to tell the brand's history aloud

events.title: Your Rival Sails West
events.body: Word arrives with the winter fleet: your rival sailed west with three hulls and a printing press, and the lane behind him is closing to everyone else. Staying east is defensible, profitable, and increasingly quiet. Following means crowding a horizon that seats two houses comfortably and three loudly, with the third writing the maps. The lane, whichever way you take it, charges the same toll in patience, scurvy, and missed letters, and issues no refunds in any currency.

choices.label: Follow west
choices.quote: Imitation: the sincerest form of logistics.

choices.label: Sell him provisions at markup
choices.quote: Arm the gold rush. Own the shovel company.

events.title: The Petition Year
events.body: Rights rhetoric floods the pamphlet presses at a copper-plate per sermon, and the throne starts reading, which is somehow worse than ignoring. Every petition cites an older petition; legitimacy has become a citation chain, and citations can be audited by people who cannot read. Your printers are the busiest workshop in three provinces and the censors have begun visiting with compliments attached.

events.title: Thirteen Candles
events.body: A distant colony drafts its own legitimacy in a room with the curtains drawn, and the prose is embarrassingly good. The crown asks which side your presses serve; the colonists ask the same question in different ink. Distance makes neutrality temporarily purchasable, and the invoice for whichever side loses will arrive by ship either way. Your presses hum through the night either way, because neutrality still requires someone to print it, and printing it is itself a position.

choices.label: Back the printers across the water
choices.quote: Bet on ideas with good distribution.

events.title: The Constitutional Convention
events.body: The rules of the new order are being written while the army waits outside, and every clause costs somebody specific. The constitutionalist waves your heir to a bench: property language, representation math, a comma with an army budget attached. Signing lends the house's name to a document that will be quoted, violated, and amended for centuries, in that order. The ink dries at exactly the speed history requires, which is to say too slowly for the army outside and too fast for everyone inside.

choices.label: Walk out on the slavery compromise
choices.quote: History rereads abstentions generously. Sometimes.

events.title: Terror Clause
events.body: The revolution has begun eating its writers, beginning with the ones who proofed the menu. Suspicion is the era's fastest-moving asset. Moderation buys distrust from both wings; radicalism buys influence with an expiration date printed on your own neck. The lists grow nightly and everyone named twice on them has developed opinions about weather. The committees request your house's papers weekly, flattering, urgent, filed under suspicion, alphabetized, which is how archives remember who was careful.

choices.label: Stay moderate
choices.quote: Trusted by neither faction: the neutral zone is narrow and downhill.

choices.label: Join the radicals
choices.quote: Heads roll. Yours included, eventually, but with seniority.

choices.label: Leave the capital for the summer

events.title: The General's Coronation
events.body: Within ten years of burning thrones, the republic hands its favorite general a crown, and the ceremony is scheduled before the debate ends. Ideals versus order, packaged as a coronation. The bankers are already repricing; the poets are choosing vocabulary carefully. The general remembers every house's vote during the ceremony and some during the war before it. The poets who praised the republic now praise the ceremony in smaller font, and the accountants have already repriced both fonts accordingly.

events.title: Continental Blockade
events.body: The empire closes a continent to trade by decree, and decrees move slower than sloops. Smuggling is now a patriotic industry with excellent margins and a felony tail. Lobbying the customs office is slower, cleaner, and priced per handshake. The blockade will fail eventually; the question is whether you'll be positioned as the proof or the cautionary tale. The customs inspectors grow rich with patriotic slowness, and the decree itself becomes a product, sold by whoever can read it first.

events.title: Rights of Persons Pamphlet
events.body: The new code needs a definition, and definitions compound into law: who counts as a person under it. The pamphleteers want patrons; the throne wants silence; the people being debated are, at this exact moment, alive, organized, and reading. Whatever your presses print tonight will be quoted in courts for two hundred years, usually by someone quoting it badly. The pamphlet ends with a sentence about consistency, which is the most dangerous word in any revolution's vocabulary, after supply.

choices.label: Print the broadest reading
choices.quote: Ink outlives every inconvenience it causes.

events.title: The Execution Shift
events.body: The square's new machine runs on tickets now, and attendance records make fine Chronicle entries — legible, dated, damning. Subscribing your name to the season list is cheap insurance and permanent wallpaper. Skipping it marks you, gently, in a register kept by people who mark everything and forget nothing except mercy. The machine, meanwhile, achieves what no edict could: standardization, punctuality, and a new meaning of the phrase seasonal subscription.

choices.label: Subscribe to the season
choices.quote: Attendance logged. The Chronicle has a long memory and no opt-out.

choices.label: Buy the box seat, say nothing ever

events.title: War Bond Gambit
events.body: Finance the revolution at five percent and the new state's spine belongs to your ledger forever afterward. Sovereign debt is immortality's uglier cousin: regimes fall, coupons persist. The risk is the one every bondholder whispers about — that the cause defaults, or worse, wins responsibly and refinances you out. The coupon clips circulate in three provinces and change hands like small printed prayers, each one a bet that tomorrow has a government.

events.title: The Occupied Library
events.body: The liberating army ships your provincial archive away for safekeeping, which is what liberation calls moving van companies. The librarians offer two paths: file formal demands through a government that may last eighteen months, or network-copy — send scribes to every sister library and rebuild by collaboration before the crates leave the department. The crates are catalogued beautifully on the way out, which is the occupier's one genuine service to scholarship, performed entirely by people who miss home.

choices.label: Network-copy everything
choices.quote: You can steal a book. Good luck stealing the reading list.

choices.label: Let it go, buy the auction lots back

events.title: Conscription Debate
events.body: The nation-in-arms drafts every heir, and the census-takers arrive with clipboards, which is the state learning everyone's birthday for the first time. Volunteering first is theater with legs: Legitimacy accrues, and the officer corps notices whose name was early on the roster. Exemptions are purchasable, visible, and remembered fondly by no one. The census follows the draft within the month, tender and exact, learning birthdays so the state can honor them and audit them in the right order.

choices.label: Equip a company instead of joining it

events.title: The Code Drafters
events.body: One rational legal code is replacing three hundred local customs, and the drafters want the house's commercial practice as a template — every clause you bless becomes national, every loophole you close closes on you too. The customary bribes, meanwhile, are finely tuned instruments of local knowledge, and codification would flatten them into mere crime. The code prints with prefaces thanking the merchants, which is how commercial practice becomes civilization, retroactively, with receipts.

choices.label: Insert one perfect clause for yourselves
choices.quote: Legislative hygiene: skip it, enjoy it, inherit it.

events.title: Exile or Emigrate
events.body: The losing faction offers the heir a choice in which neither option is good: exile with honor and no assets, or emigration with assets and no story. The émigré nobility sells family silver abroad at prices that make appraisers wince, and the silver remembers where it came from the way silver does — via provenance, eventually, at auction. Both options include a courteous escort to the border, which is the new regime's politeness, and the old regime's, which says something about regimes.

events.title: The Tricolor or the Old Flag
events.body: The house sign gets repainted mid-decade, and trade partners pick a side either way, politely, while repricing contracts. Flags are marketing for governments and credit ratings for houses. Whichever cloth flies over the counting house, half the customer base will consider it a statement, and statements settle in cash. The sign painter is the only person guaranteed employment under either government, which makes him, quietly, the era's most stable fortune.

choices.label: Fly both, seasonally
choices.quote: Brand flexibility, revolutionary edition.

events.title: Suffrage Audit
events.body: The lineage's own council meets to decide who votes in the lineage's own council, because revolutions are awkward indoors. Franchise proposals circulate with footnotes; the household staff have developed unexpected interest in quorum rules. Whatever precedent set here will be cited at dinner for a century, usually by the losing side. The household learns the new math of franchises overnight, mostly correctly, entirely defensively, with footnotes prepared for dinner.

events.title: The Ledger Becomes the Relic
events.body: The Custodian arrives in lawyerly mode with the first constitutional-era account book — the state's debts bound as an heirloom — and asks where the fire brand should be filed relative to it. Her dialogue has aged from proverb to case law. The revolution's creditors and its patriots both want the ledger notarized, which is the sound of history discovering escrow.

choices.label: Ask the Custodian her ruling
choices.quote: Precedent, she says, is just gossip with tenure.

events.title: The Rival Ennobles
events.body: Your rival takes a title from the emperor you opposed, and the portrait goes up with the ribbon prominent. His descendants still salute him; yours still argue about the argument. The court inverts your position like a lens: his name appears in grants, yours in petitions. History's scoreboard updates nightly and accepts no appeals. The portrait hangs at an angle that catches the light, which curators call composition and historians call propaganda, gently, over tea.

choices.label: Marry into the new nobility anyway

events.title: The Luddite Visit
events.body: A mob stands before your automated frames with hammers and a petition, historically in that order of effectiveness. Their math is honest: machines took piecework. Your math is honest too: competitors automate or die.

choices.label: Automate harder
choices.quote: Efficiency won the meeting; the street hasn't adjourned.

choices.label: Co-ownership deal
choices.quote: Workers as shareholders: radical, solvent.

choices.label: Private guards on the roof
choices.quote: The Peterloo option. History files it under 'P.'

events.title: The Child Labor Vote
events.body: Parliament puts reform on the floor: minimum ages, maximum hours. Your mills run on small hands and larger profits. The factories will relocate if regulated; the children will remain if the factories do.

choices.label: Support reform
choices.quote: Morality as infrastructure investment.

choices.label: Lobby against
choices.quote: The opium of the boardroom.

choices.label: Comply nominally; 'family apprenticeships.'
choices.quote: Loopholes are compliance with extra steps.

events.title: Railway Mania
events.body: Every town wants a line, every speculator wants a station, and share prices have detached from anything as vulgar as terrain. Building anyway adds network value; pulling out preserves capital and reputation for the crash.

choices.label: Build the trunk line
choices.quote: Railways: capital-intensive miracles, occasionally bankrupt.

choices.label: Sell shares into the mania
choices.quote: Greater fool theory, gauge-standardized.

choices.label: Finance only routes with freight
choices.quote: Boring tonnage beats glamorous passengers.

events.title: The Smog Audit
events.body: A physician publishes mortality statistics linking your works and air to lung deaths, complete with names. The works employ half the county; the county is dying measurably.

choices.label: Install scrubbers
choices.quote: Filters: expensive partial honesty.

choices.label: Dispute the statistics
choices.quote: Doubt is a product; this one's defective.

choices.label: Relocate works, rename town
choices.quote: Externalize geographically.

events.title: The Engine Patent Trap
events.body: Your engineer's high-efficiency valve design is blocked by a patent thicket held by a competitor who manufactures nothing, litigates everything, and wears the word 'innovation' as a costume.

choices.label: Pay the licensing toll
choices.quote: Patent trolls predate the internet by 170 years.

choices.label: Design around it
choices.quote: Reverse engineering: free speech with blueprints.

choices.label: Challenge the patent in court
choices.quote: Win big, lose years.

events.title: The Great Exhibition Temptation
events.body: The world's fair invites your machinery to a glass palace beside the world's machinery. Displays cost fortunes; impressions convert to export orders; espionage comes with the visitor tickets.

choices.label: Show the flagship engine
choices.quote: Soft power, torque-rated.

choices.label: Show last year's engine
choices.quote: Planned obsolescence on display.

choices.label: Skip the fair; poach exhibited engineers
choices.quote: Exhibits walk away carrying your R&D.

events.title: The Union Recognition Question
events.body: The craft unions propose collective bargaining: orderly strikes, written procedures, no hammers. An alternative to mob math exists, and management finds it almost as frightening as mobs.

choices.label: Recognize the union
choices.quote: Industrial relations: marriage without romance.

choices.label: Refuse; blacklist organizers
choices.quote: Suppress today, detonate quarterly.

choices.label: Company welfare program instead
choices.quote: Paternalism: the subscription to loyalty.

events.title: The Boiler Explosion
events.body: A works boiler fails during shift change. Casualties, inquiries, and the discovery that safety inspections were 'deferred for throughput.' The inspector general enjoys paperwork the way boilers enjoy pressure.

choices.label: Full disclosure, full compensation
choices.quote: Accountability: bitter, curative.

choices.label: Settle quietly, fix quietly
choices.quote: Quiet settlements set precedents quietly.

choices.label: Blame the fired stoker
choices.quote: Scapegoating: legacy incident management.

events.title: Coal Futures, Sunlight Derivatives
events.body: The exchange lists coal futures and suddenly stockpiled Carboniferous sunshine trades at a premium on winter forecasts. Hedging protects margins; speculation protects egos.

choices.label: Hedge production
choices.quote: Risk moved, not removed. That was always the deal.

choices.label: Corner regional supply
choices.quote: Monopoly: the oldest sport, various imports.

choices.label: Stay out of financials; dig coal
choices.quote: Productive capital: quaint, occasionally survives.

events.title: The Emigration Steamship
events.body: Famine and engines push millions toward the western hemisphere; shipping lines need capital and souls need berths. Passenger fares are thin; cargo is fat; the era's legal distinctions between the two are load-bearing.

choices.label: Carry passengers humanely
choices.quote: Berths below, dignity above deck.

choices.label: Cargo only
choices.quote: Neutrality: profitable, archaeological.

choices.label: Finance destination towns
choices.quote: Colonize the balance sheet.

events.title: The Time Zone Problem
events.body: Rail timetables collide with local suns: every town keeps its own noon and the junctions are chaos. Standardize time and the railways own the clock; leave it local and crashes schedule themselves.

choices.label: Impose standard time
choices.quote: Nature objected. Trains proceeded.

choices.label: Dual-clock stations
choices.quote: Compromise measured in missed connections.

choices.label: Sell the timetable software
choices.quote: Whoever writes the schedule charges rent on the day.

events.title: The Crystal Palace Debt
events.body: The exhibition left a debt, a park, and a national myth. Creditors want the land sold; reformers want it kept public forever; both cite the same founding brochure.

choices.label: Sell to developers
choices.quote: Glass palaces become glass towers. Cycle confirmed.

choices.label: Keep it public, subsidize
choices.quote: Civic monuments: liabilities that appreciate culturally.

choices.label: Endowment model: leases fund upkeep
choices.quote: Monetize the gift shop, preserve the myth.

events.title: The Assembly Line Bargain
events.body: An efficiency consultant offers to cut build time in half by making every worker perform one motion eight hundred times daily. Output doubles. So does the particular silence of people completing sentences nobody started.

choices.label: Adopt the line
choices.quote: The moving conveyor: humanity, JIT.

choices.label: Adopt with rotation
choices.quote: Boredom diversified. Marginally.

choices.label: Refuse; craft positioning
choices.quote: Artisanal: a luxury hedge.

events.title: Crash of '29, Position Check
events.body: Tickers print fiction downward. The portfolio evaporates between lunch and afternoon coffee. Sell at the bottom for certainty, hold for recovery, or buy while panic is on clearance — history's favorite multiple-choice. [Flag: doubling down sets the Accelerationista lineage flag, referenced Era 11.]

choices.label: Sell everything
choices.quote: Certainty purchased at a discount to dignity.

choices.label: Hold
choices.quote: The market recovered; careers didn't.

choices.label: Double down
choices.quote: Buying the century's dip. Terms apply.

events.title: Total War Mobilization
events.body: The second world war requests the whole factory, the whole ledger, and eventually the whole family tree. Conversion to war output pays in contracts and spends in sons.

choices.label: Full conversion
choices.quote: Arsenal of anything, overtime.

choices.label: Civilian production, quietly
choices.quote: Neutrality: profitable until indexed.

choices.label: Run R&D for the war department
choices.quote: The labs came back strange.

events.title: The Suburb Contract
events.body: Mass housing: identical streets, mortgages thirty years long, cars counted as infrastructure. Builders want capital; the nation wants normalcy; the ledger wants a category for 'the good life.'

choices.label: Finance the subdivisions
choices.quote: Dreams, tract-priced, interest-bearing.

choices.label: Build urban transit instead
choices.quote: The road not taken, fare-boxed.

choices.label: Both, weighted
choices.quote: Hedged lifestyle portfolio.

events.title: The Company Town Rehearsal
events.body: Operations proposes building housing, stores, and schools for workers — company script, company doctor, company mercy. Efficiency theorists call it integration; preachers call it feudalism with electricity.

choices.label: Build the town
choices.quote: Everything for the worker except options.

choices.label: Wages only; let towns emerge
choices.quote: Cash is freedom-shaped, if enough.

choices.label: Union-free covenants in deeds
choices.quote: Contractual silence, recorded county-wide.

events.title: The Management Consulting Wave
events.body: Advisors in gray suits propose restructuring by organizational chart: layers, matrices, synergies. Productivity charts improve immediately because the charts are the consultants' deliverable.

choices.label: Hire the firm
choices.quote: Synergy: invoiced.

choices.label: Fire the firm mid-engagement
choices.quote: The report was the product; skip to savings.

choices.label: Adopt the org chart, ignore the strategy
choices.quote: Structure without direction: modern art.

events.title: Petro-Diplomacy
events.body: A desert concession offers oil for decades at terms that made previous empires blush, payable in guarantees, bases, and selective blindness. The wellhead is distant; the dependencies are local.

choices.label: Sign the concession
choices.quote: Liquid power, solid entanglements.

choices.label: Demand majority ownership
choices.quote: Partnership: negotiations eventually conducted via coups.

choices.label: Invest in efficiency instead
choices.quote: The least sexy barrel is the one not drilled.

events.title: The Consumer Engine
events.body: Marketing proposes planned obsolescence: design products to fail attractively. Growth becomes structurally guaranteed and entropy becomes a line item disguised as fashion.

choices.label: Adopt planned obsolescence
choices.quote: Warranty periods as destiny.

choices.label: Build 'lifetime' goods at premium
choices.quote: Durability: contrarian, defensible.

choices.label: Obsolesce by software later; hardware honest now
choices.quote: The upgrade treadmill goes virtual.

events.title: The First Television Election
events.body: Campaign strategy pivots from platforms to lighting. A rival candidate loses because he sweats on camera, which everyone notices and nobody says for sixty years.

choices.label: Invest in studio
choices.quote: Democracy, key-lit.

choices.label: Policy-only campaign
choices.quote: Correct, unelectable, archival.

choices.label: Weaponize the opponent's footage
choices.quote: Attack media: pre-loaded, professionally graded.

events.title: Bretton Woods Seat
events.body: The postwar order is being seated at a hotel and someone must host the currency peg. Hosting earns seigniorage; joining earns stability; both earn obligations denominated in other countries' crises.

choices.label: Host and anchor
choices.quote: Reserve status: privilege with recurring fees.

choices.label: Join as client
choices.quote: Stability sublet from someone else's central bank.

choices.label: Propose a neutral settlement unit
choices.quote: Multilateral idealism; the delegates politely tabled it.

events.title: The Highway Act
events.body: A national interstate system: armies of earthmoving, cities bisected, motels budding along the ribbon, rail dying prettily. The justification is defense; the effect is sprawl with a budget code.

choices.label: Champion the interstates
choices.quote: Concrete arteries, urban scars.

choices.label: Fund rail modernization instead
choices.quote: The electrification that might have been.

choices.label: Highways plus preserved urban rail
choices.quote: Expensive both-ways. Historians hopeful.

events.title: The Memory Mugging, Proto
events.body: An executive augmented with experimental memory aids is mugged in an alley for the hardware — his appointment book, passwords, and childhood, gone in fifteen seconds. Reconstruction begins from corporate records, which is to say: whoever reconstructs him defines him. [Chronicle callback mechanic debuts here; full version Era 9.]

choices.label: Reconstruct from Chronicle entries only
choices.quote: The family archive as backup drive.

choices.label: Reconstruct from corporate files
choices.quote: The company remembers what it profited from.

choices.label: Let him rebuild unaided
choices.quote: Blank-slate insurance policy.

events.title: Total Mobilization
events.body: The conversion order lands on Friday: consumer lines become munitions by Monday, and efficiency arrives wearing a uniform. The same plant that made tractors will make tanks, then washing machines, and the tooling changes faster than the menus. Posters appear everywhere exhorting everyone to make do and mend, designed by the same ad men who sold the tractors. The time clocks multiply, the whistles govern whole towns, and the calendar acquires a military accent it will never fully lose.

events.title: Ration Book Heir
events.body: Children learn ounces before words; butter becomes a currency with a black-market yield curve. The ration stamps were designed by advertising men, which is how you know morale is a managed product. Paying for butter in Legitimacy is quiet arithmetic everyone does at the counter and nobody logs, until someone does. The household keeps a chart of margins above the pantry door, updated weekly, which the children assume is a game until they understand money.

choices.label: Open the estate gates to neighbors

events.title: The Codebreaking Room
events.body: A hut full of brilliant misfits reads the enemy's mail and asks only for room, board, and absolute silence afterward. The Knowledge surge is real and enormous; the secrecy oath freezes their patents for decades, and the winning side files the whole breakthrough under never mind. One of them solves puzzles for the war effort and crossword puzzles for the soul.

choices.label: Route them to patent law instead

events.title: Two Fronts, One Bloodline
events.body: Cousins hold both sides of a border that used to be a fence, and the Chronicle must hide nothing and forgive everything, because both cousins will read it. Every letter is censored twice, once by each army, by officers who share an aunt. Family archives become contraband with genealogy. The censor on one side reads the letter first; the censor on the other reads it second; both underline the same sentence about Aunt Ruth.

choices.label: Run letters between the cousins
choices.quote: Postal service. Extremely local. Potentially fatal.

events.title: The Home Factory Shift
events.body: Whoever stays behind runs the line, and the line runs twenty-four hours: wages climb, hazards climb faster, and a permanent change settles into who the house employs. The foreman's daughter is now running a shift the foreman couldn't. Nobody wrote this down as progress yet, but the payroll did. The night shift starts keeping its own minutes, and the factory learns the sound of people who have discovered they are essential, permanently, at volume.

events.title: The Bombing Ledger
events.body: Staff officers present the choice in columns: the rival's plants or the rival's rail yards, precision measured in tonnage. Entropy doesn't check passports on the way down, and the ledger's clean arithmetic hides a footer nobody prints. Both columns win the campaign. The footer is billed to the peace, at interest. The staff college teaches the campaign for decades afterward, admiring the columns, and assigns the footer as optional reading, which is how staff colleges work.

events.title: POW Parcel Exchange
events.body: Small humanity is available at reasonable logistics rates: parcels of socks, tobacco, and milk powder routed through neutral channels, priced in shipping tons the war desperately needs elsewhere. Return on investment is negligible. The Legitimacy is real but soft. Do the math and the answer is no; do anything else and the answer is send them. The logistics board grumbles about tonnage for a week and then stops mentioning it, which is the closest thing the war produces to grace.

choices.label: Send the parcels
choices.quote: Negligible ROI. Correct anyway. Keep the receipt.

events.title: The Occupation Payroll
events.body: Coins stamped for occupied territories arrive in a crate with an instruction sheet. Spend them and the house inherits the stamp — every transaction a small endorsement, filed forever in metal. Refuse them and the payroll fails, the workers go unpaid, and the refusal is also a statement, just quieter and colder. The coins circulate for decades after, found in gardens, mint-fresh, each one a small museum of the question of who was paying whom.

events.title: Displaced Experts Offer
events.body: Rocketry scientists are handed over at a checkpoint with a checklist of the labs they built, their handwriting meticulous, their futures negotiable. Knowledge arrives doubled; so does the moral debt, itemized in appendices nobody signs. Every clean room they fill has a previous tenant whose name the transfer papers spell approximately. The rocketry they bring works beautifully, on schedule, and lands, eventually, somewhere nobody planned, which is the entire era in one appendix.

events.title: The Ceasefire Telegram
events.body: Peace arrives three seconds late to your front — the telegram timestamped, the orders still traveling, the last hour of the war fully documented and entirely optional in hindsight. Choose which final order you gave: the record keeps whatever you sign, and the historians will weigh your signature against the clock. The last casualty and the last medal share a timestamp, filed together, which some clerk considers tidy and posterity considers obscene.

choices.label: Halt at once, telegram or not
Take the ridge before midnight
choices.quote: Medals issued posthumously have excellent timing.

events.title: War Debt Write-off
events.body: The creditor nation forgives nothing and the debtor nation prints everything; pick a side of the ledger to stand on. Creditors keep the moral high ground and slowly lose the money supply's respect. Printers keep the money flowing and meet the inflation that respects nothing. Both sides call their choice responsibility. The negotiators shake hands across a table bolted to nothing, and both delegations cable home the word responsible, meaning opposite things, correctly.

events.title: Victory Parade Inventory
events.body: Triumph costs more than the war — banners, brass bands, a mile of bunting, crowds that must be transported, fed, and photographed. Parades are infrastructure that applauds. The ledger balances in Legitimacy, a currency accepted exclusively at ceremonies, and the maintenance bill for the memorial arrives annually, forever, punctually. The bunting outlasts the veterans' pensions in storage, which tells you the true comparative budget lines of triumph and obligation.

choices.label: Skip the parade, fund the veterans
choices.quote: Quieter. Better. Unphotographed. Correct.

events.title: The Camps Report
events.body: Liberation footage enters the Chronicle: dated, catalogued, undeniable. Some heirs refuse to read it, and the refusal is itself logged, timestamped, attributable. There is no option here that preserves comfort. There is only the option that determines what the archive says you were when the evidence arrived. The projection room stays warm late into the night, heirs arriving alone, leaving slower, and the Chronicle logs attendance without comment, which is comment enough.

choices.label: Read it. Enter it. Teach it.
File it unread
choices.quote: The archive notes the filing method. The archive always notes.

events.title: Radar Dividend
events.body: Wartime sensors go looking for peacetime jobs and find them absurdly well: microwave ovens, air traffic control, weather screens. The spin-off auction is the war's refund check, payable in products nobody asked for that everybody will want. The engineers who swore the oath are quietly unsworn and extremely employable. The kitchen counter becomes a consumer electronics showroom within five years, and nobody alive connects the microwave to the hut with the locked door. Everybody should.

events.title: Treaty Signatures at Dawn
events.body: The peace table redraws the map in pencil before anyone has coffee, and the house picks which border its grandchildren will defend. Every line on the paper is somebody's kitchen. The delegate offering you a pen has excellent handwriting and no intention of remembering your objections after breakfast. The pencil line becomes a fence, the fence becomes a policy, and the policy becomes a generation's geography, drawn by a delegate needing a win before lunch.

choices.label: Take the humane border
choices.quote: Maps are promises. Pick the one you'd keep sober.

events.title: Handoff in the Bunker
events.body: During the evacuation the Custodian carries the ledger through three corridors, two sirens, and one floodgate, and ages decades inside a single scene — the jokes arriving later, thinner, better. She hands the satchel to the heir without ceremony and says the relic is heavier than it looks, which is not a statement about paper. The bunker lights flicker in agreement.

choices.label: Ask her to keep carrying it
choices.quote: She agrees. She notes who asked. Noting is her other skill.

choices.label: Copy the ledger first, then carry

events.title: Opposite Flags
events.body: The mirror completes: your rival salutes the flag you oppose, precisely, visibly, with photographs. Two lineages trained to opposite uniforms, marching toward the same Tuesday. Whatever this ends, both houses will explain it differently for a century, and the difference between the explanations will be the actual inheritance. The photographs develop slowly, in both capitals, and arrive at the same conclusion from opposite darkrooms, which the Chronicle files under symmetry.

choices.label: Record the divergence plainly
choices.quote: The Chronicle takes both versions. It always takes both versions.

events.title: The Censor's Evening
events.body: V-mail reduces a soldier's letters home to grams of microfilm, which the censor reads at volume before anyone else does — including the ones addressed to your own household, filed under return address because that is how filing works. A sergeant describes the war plainly and asks the censor, politely, to let it through anyway. The stamp is available in two flavors: approved, or shredded with regrets logged.

choices.label: Approve the plain accounts
choices.quote: Morale, some say, is just news delivered on time.

choices.label: Copy the sergeant's letter into the Chronicle

events.title: The Clock to Two
events.body: Intelligence compresses the timeline: the doomsday clock moves to two minutes. Weapon programs promise deterrence through brightness; treaties promise it through signatures. Both are theories of mind about people who own suns.

choices.label: Launch the secret program
choices.quote: Peace through superior megatonnage. Terms: see armageddon.

choices.label: Sign the test treaty
choices.quote: Verified restraint; unverifiable intentions.

choices.label: Declare a moratorium, inspect nothing
choices.quote: Strategic ambiguity, budget-friendly.

events.title: The Reactor Gamble
events.body: Commercial nuclear offers baseload power without smoke — the era's cleanest energy and dirtiest liability, packaged with a containment dome and an insurance act.

choices.label: Build the fleet
choices.quote: Sunlight, bottled, monthly statements.

choices.label: Refuse; coal continues
choices.quote: The devil you meter.

choices.label: One demonstration plant, watched closely
choices.quote: Pilot programs: anxiety with instrumentation.

events.title: Crisis at Thirty Seconds
events.body: A false alarm, a real fleet, a hotline, and a decision window measured in the time it takes a person to realize they are deciding. The officer on duty can escalate, de-escalate, or vomit; only two are options.

choices.label: Hold the line, verify
choices.quote: The right stuff, thanklessly employed.

choices.label: Escalate posture one notch
choices.quote: Nervous systems worldwide concur: inadvisable.

choices.label: Publish the failure transparently
choices.quote: Radical transparency about near-apocalypse. Historians shaken.

events.title: The Nonproliferation Ask
events.body: An allied state requests fissile shares for a 'peaceful program,' phrased exactly as every weapons program is phrased before the parade. Denial costs alliance; supply costs the clock.

choices.label: Supply under inspection
choices.quote: Controlled spread: an oxymoron with meetings.

choices.label: Deny firmly
choices.quote: Friends will call it betrayal; grandchildren, gratitude.

choices.label: Offer their own reactor, fuel-supplied, return-enriched
choices.quote: The closed fuel cycle: diplomacy with plumbing.

events.title: Fallout Comes Due
events.body: Downwind communities file claims; the map of isotopes matches the map of childhood cancers. The tests were legal, necessary according to the briefing, and measurable in bone.

choices.label: Settle the claims
choices.quote: Compensation: late, insufficient, moral arithmetic.

choices.label: Classify the epidemiology
choices.quote: Some data achieves half-life.

choices.label: Fund the hospitals, don't discuss causes
choices.quote: Care without confession.

events.title: The Mutual Assured Ledger
events.body: Strategists propose buying invulnerability twice over: enough warheads that an attack means your own deletion, priced annually forever. The logic is flawless and the board flinches at the P&L of omnicide-as-service.

choices.label: Full triad procurement
choices.quote: Insurance you hope voids itself.

choices.label: Minimum deterrent
choices.quote: Cheaper, less certain, sleep-neutral.

choices.label: Divert to civil defense
choices.quote: Fallout shelters: comforting, arithmetically meaningless.

events.title: The Satellite Window
events.body: A rocket opportunity: orbit the reconnaissance satellite for security, the telescope for knowledge, or the broadcast payload for hearts and minds. The launch window forgives no committee.

choices.label: Reconnaissance bird
choices.quote: Trust, but photograph.

choices.label: Orbital telescope
choices.quote: The universe, peer-reviewed from above.

choices.label: Broadcast transmitter
choices.quote: Hearts and minds, uplinked.

events.title: The Scientists' Letter
events.body: The veterans who built the first device circulate a letter begging control of what they enabled, signed by people whose guilt has finally achieved escape velocity. Management finds their moral authority operationally inconvenient.

choices.label: Amplify the letter
choices.quote: Makers as whistleblowers: accountability origin story.

choices.label: Suppress it internally
choices.quote: Leaked anyway. Veterans leak.

choices.label: Fund the arms-control bureau they propose
